title: fix: Bluetooth audio dropouts on Macs with Broadcom BT
author: coquer
body:
- Disable btusb autosuspend on Macs with Broadcom Bluetooth — autosuspend repeatedly power-cycles the controller between transmissions, causing periodic audio dropouts. Fixed via /etc/modprobe.d/btusb-autosuspend.conf (install/hardware/apple/fix-btusb-autosuspend.sh), wired into install/hardware/all.sh.

- Cap Bluetooth codec negotiation to aac, sbc_xq, sbc on the same hardware — AAC re-encoding on these Broadcom controllers is timing-sensitive and stutters under Wi-Fi/BT antenna contention (both radios share one antenna). AAC stays first in the list so working devices (e.g. AirPods) aren't downgraded; it's a fallback net, not a priority swap away from AAC. Shipped as a WirePlumber fragment (default/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/bluez-prefer-sbc.conf), applied user-side via install/user/hardware/apple/fix-bluetooth-codec.sh, wired into install/user/all.sh.

- Both fixes are gated on the same Broadcom Wi-Fi/BT combo detection already used by fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh (T2 PCI ID or Apple DMI vendor + brcmfmac PCI ID list) — Macs only, no effect elsewhere.

- Added migrations (1787262778.sh, 1787263050.sh) so existing installs pick up both fixes, idempotent.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,10 @@
+## bluez5.codecs is an ordered whitelist: it both restricts negotiation to the
+## codecs listed and sets their preference order. Broadcom Bluetooth
+## controllers (found in Intel and Apple Silicon-era MacBooks) stutter and
+## drop out worst on aptX/LDAC, especially under Wi-Fi/Bluetooth antenna
+## contention, so those are left out entirely. AAC stays first so devices
+## like AirPods that already work fine on it aren't downgraded to SBC.
+
+monitor.bluez.properties = {
+  bluez5.codecs = [ aac, sbc_xq, sbc ]
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
+# Linux's btusb driver autosuspends the Bluetooth controller by default,
+# repeatedly power-cycling it, which shows up as periodic audio dropouts and
+# stutter on Bluetooth headsets/speakers connected to Macs whose Bluetooth is
+# USB-attached - a problem macOS doesn't have since its own driver doesn't
+# autosuspend the same way. This only fixes machines whose Bluetooth is
+# actually on btusb; see the exclusion and inclusion notes below.
+sys_vendor="$(cat /sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor 2>/dev/null || true)"
+
+# Bluetooth over PCIe (hci_bcm4377, on T2 Macs and Apple Silicon Macs running
+# Asahi) isn't on btusb, so this option has no controller to act on there.
+# Check the Bluetooth function's own PCI ID rather than proxying through the
+# T2 bridge chip - the bridge tells you a machine has PCIe Bluetooth, but its
+# absence doesn't tell you the Bluetooth is on USB (Apple Silicon has PCIe
+# Bluetooth with no T2 bridge at all). lspci -nn matches past the point
+# grep -q would stop reading, so a match further down its output still needs
+# the full pipe drained.
+if lspci -nn | grep -E "14e4:(5fa0|5f69|5f71|5f72)" >/dev/null; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+# 14e4:43a0/4331 are the 2012-2015 Macs on the out-of-tree wl driver
+# (install/hardware/fix-bcm43xx.sh); the rest are the brcmfmac-driven Wi-Fi
+# IDs from install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh. Both groups'
+# Bluetooth is a Broadcom part on USB.
+if [[ $sys_vendor == Apple* ]] &&
+  lspci -nn | grep -E "14e4:(43a0|4331|43ba|43bb|43bc|43a3|43dc|4464|4488)" >/dev/null; then
+  echo "Detected a Mac with USB-attached Broadcom Bluetooth; disabling btusb autosuspend"
+
+  mkdir -p /etc/modprobe.d
+  echo "options btusb enable_autosuspend=n" > /etc/modprobe.d/btusb-autosuspend.conf
+fi

@@ -9,6 +9,7 @@ run_logged "$OMARCHY_INSTALL/user/hardware/asus/fix-mic.sh"
 run_logged "$OMARCHY_INSTALL/user/hardware/framework/fix-f13-amd-audio-input.sh"
 run_logged "$OMARCHY_INSTALL/user/hardware/dell/xps13-text-scaling.sh"
 run_logged "$OMARCHY_INSTALL/user/hardware/fix-nouveau-cursor.sh"
+run_logged "$OMARCHY_INSTALL/user/hardware/apple/fix-bluetooth-codec.sh"
 
 run_logged "$OMARCHY_INSTALL/user/default-keyring.sh"
 run_logged "$OMARCHY_INSTALL/user/mise.sh"

@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@
+# Cap Bluetooth codecs to AAC/SBC-XQ/SBC on Macs with the older Broadcom
+# Bluetooth parts named below. See
+# default/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/bluez-codec-cap.conf for why. Unlike
+# the btusb autosuspend fix, this targets the chip family, not the transport
+# it's on - T2 Macs (PCIe hci_bcm4377) get it alongside the USB-attached
+# ones, since codec negotiation happens over the Bluetooth link either way.
+# Apple Silicon Macs also use hci_bcm4377, but a newer chip generation
+# (4377/4378/4387/4388) this fix isn't about, so their Wi-Fi PCI IDs are
+# deliberately left out of the match below.
+sys_vendor="$(cat /sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor 2>/dev/null || true)"
+
+if lspci -nn | grep "106b:180[12]" >/dev/null ||
+  { [[ $sys_vendor == Apple* ]] &&
+    lspci -nn | grep -E "14e4:(43a0|4331|43ba|43bb|43bc|43a3|43dc|4464|4488)" >/dev/null; }; then
+  mkdir -p ~/.config/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/
+  cp "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/bluez-codec-cap.conf" ~/.config/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/
+fi

@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@
+echo "Disable btusb autosuspend on Macs with USB-attached Broadcom Bluetooth"
+
+# The install-time fix only reaches machines set up after it shipped. See
+# install/hardware/apple/fix-btusb-autosuspend.sh for the dropout it fixes,
+# for why T2 Macs are excluded, and for where this PCI ID list comes from.
+dmi_vendor="${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_DMI_VENDOR:-/sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor}"
+conf="${OMARCHY_BTUSB_AUTOSUSPEND_CONF:-/etc/modprobe.d/btusb-autosuspend.conf}"
+
+if lspci -nn | grep -E "14e4:(5fa0|5f69|5f71|5f72)" >/dev/null; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+sys_vendor="$(cat "$dmi_vendor" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+
+if ! { [[ $sys_vendor == Apple* ]] &&
+  lspci -nn | grep -E "14e4:(43a0|4331|43ba|43bb|43bc|43a3|43dc|4464|4488)" >/dev/null; }; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+[[ -f $conf ]] && exit 0
+
+sudo mkdir -p "$(dirname "$conf")"
+echo "options btusb enable_autosuspend=n" | sudo tee "$conf" >/dev/null
+
+omarchy-state set reboot-required

@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@
+echo "Cap Bluetooth codecs to AAC/SBC-XQ/SBC on Macs with Broadcom Bluetooth"
+
+# The install-time fix only reaches machines set up after it shipped. See
+# install/user/hardware/apple/fix-bluetooth-codec.sh for the dropout it fixes
+# and for where this list of brcmfmac PCI IDs comes from.
+dmi_vendor="${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_DMI_VENDOR:-/sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor}"
+conf="$HOME/.config/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/bluez-codec-cap.conf"
+
+sys_vendor="$(cat "$dmi_vendor" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+
+if ! lspci -nn | grep "106b:180[12]" >/dev/null &&
+  ! { [[ $sys_vendor == Apple* ]] &&
+    lspci -nn | grep -E "14e4:(43a0|4331|43ba|43bb|43bc|43a3|43dc|4464|4488)" >/dev/null; }; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+[[ -f $conf ]] && exit 0
+
+mkdir -p "$(dirname "$conf")"
+cp "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/bluez-codec-cap.conf" "$conf"
+
+# WirePlumber only reads conf.d on startup, and it's already running in this
+# session with the old codec list cached; restart it so the cap applies now
+# instead of waiting for the next login.
+omarchy-restart-audio >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

@@ -0,0 +1,127 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
+
+leaf="$ROOT/install/user/hardware/apple/fix-bluetooth-codec.sh"
+fragment="$ROOT/default/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/bluez-codec-cap.conf"
+all="$ROOT/install/user/all.sh"
+migration="$ROOT/migrations/1787263050.sh"
+
+grep -q 'apple/fix-bluetooth-codec.sh' "$all" ||
+  fail "the codec cap runs during user setup"
+pass "the codec cap runs during user setup"
+
+grep -q 'bluez5.codecs' "$fragment" || fail "the fragment sets bluez5.codecs"
+grep -q '\baac\b' "$fragment" ||
+  fail "the fragment keeps AAC so working devices like AirPods are not downgraded"
+pass "the shipped fragment keeps AAC ahead of SBC"
+
+test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT
+
+stub_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
+calls="$test_tmp/calls.log"
+mkdir -p "$stub_bin" "$test_tmp/dmi"
+
+cat >"$stub_bin/lspci" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+
+if (( ${T2_HARDWARE:-0} == 1 )); then
+  echo '01:00.0 Bridge [0680]: Apple Inc. T2 Security Chip [106b:1801]'
+fi
+if [[ -n ${WIFI_ID:-} ]]; then
+  echo "03:00.0 Network controller [0280]: Broadcom Inc. Wireless [14e4:$WIFI_ID]"
+fi
+for _ in {1..4096}; do
+  echo '02:00.0 Host bridge [0600]: Filler Device [ffff:0000]'
+done
+SH
+
+cat >"$stub_bin/omarchy-restart-audio" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+
+printf 'omarchy-restart-audio\n' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+SH
+
+chmod +x "$stub_bin"/*
+
+conf() { printf '%s/.config/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/bluez-codec-cap.conf' "$1"; }
+
+run_leaf() {
+  local vendor="$1" wifi_id="${2:-}" t2="${3:-0}"
+  local home="$test_tmp/home"
+  rm -rf "$home"
+  mkdir -p "$home"
+  printf '%s' "$vendor" >"$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor"
+
+  local script="$test_tmp/leaf.sh"
+  sed "s|/sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor|$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor|g" "$leaf" >"$script"
+
+  WIFI_ID="$wifi_id" T2_HARDWARE="$t2" HOME="$home" \
+    OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" \
+    bash -eE -o pipefail -c 'source "$1"' bash "$script" </dev/null
+
+  printf '%s' "$home"
+}
+
+home=$(run_leaf "Apple Inc." 4488 1)
+diff -q "$(conf "$home")" "$fragment" >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
+  fail "a T2 Mac gets the codec cap" "$(ls -R "$home" 2>&1)"
+pass "a T2 Mac gets the codec cap"
+
+home=$(run_leaf "Apple Inc." 43ba 0)
+[[ -f $(conf "$home") ]] || fail "a Mac without a T2 gets the codec cap"
+pass "a Mac without a T2 gets the codec cap"
+
+home=$(run_leaf "Apple Inc." 43a0 0)
+[[ -f $(conf "$home") ]] || fail "a BCM4360 Mac gets the codec cap"
+pass "a BCM4360 Mac gets the codec cap"
+
+home=$(run_leaf "Apple Inc." 4331 0)
+[[ -f $(conf "$home") ]] || fail "a BCM4331 Mac gets the codec cap"
+pass "a BCM4331 Mac gets the codec cap"
+
+# Apple Silicon Macs run Bluetooth on a newer chip generation this fix isn't
+# about, so their Wi-Fi IDs are deliberately absent from the match list.
+home=$(run_leaf "Apple Inc." 4425 0)
+[[ ! -f $(conf "$home") ]] || fail "an Apple Silicon Mac is left alone; its Bluetooth chip is a different generation"
+pass "an Apple Silicon Mac is left alone; its Bluetooth chip is a different generation"
+
+home=$(run_leaf "LENOVO" 43ba 0)
+[[ ! -f $(conf "$home") ]] || fail "non-Apple hardware is left alone"
+pass "non-Apple hardware is left alone"
+
+run_migration() {
+  local vendor="$1" wifi_id="${2:-}" t2="${3:-0}" home="$4"
+  printf '%s' "$vendor" >"$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor"
+  : >"$calls"
+
+  WIFI_ID="$wifi_id" T2_HARDWARE="$t2" HOME="$home" \
+    OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" TEST_LOG="$calls" \
+    OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_DMI_VENDOR="$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor" \
+    bash -euo pipefail "$migration" >/dev/null
+}
+
+home="$test_tmp/migrate-home"
+rm -rf "$home"
+mkdir -p "$home"
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 43ba 0 "$home"
+diff -q "$(conf "$home")" "$fragment" >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
+  fail "the migration fixes an install that never got the codec cap" "$(ls -R "$home" 2>&1)"
+grep -Fq 'omarchy-restart-audio' "$calls" ||
+  fail "the migration restarts audio so the cap applies to the running session" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration fixes an install and restarts audio to apply it now"
+
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 43ba 0 "$home"
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] || fail "a repaired install is left untouched" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration is idempotent"
+
+home="$test_tmp/skip-home"
+rm -rf "$home"
+mkdir -p "$home"
+run_migration "LENOVO" 43ba 0 "$home"
+[[ ! -e $(conf "$home") ]] || fail "the migration skips non-Apple hardware" "$(cat "$(conf "$home")")"
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] || fail "the migration escalates nothing on unaffected hardware" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration skips hardware without the combo Broadcom chip"

@@ -0,0 +1,170 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
+
+leaf="$ROOT/install/hardware/apple/fix-btusb-autosuspend.sh"
+all="$ROOT/install/hardware/all.sh"
+migration="$ROOT/migrations/1787262778.sh"
+
+grep -q 'apple/fix-btusb-autosuspend.sh' "$all" ||
+  fail "the btusb autosuspend fix runs during hardware setup"
+pass "the btusb autosuspend fix runs during hardware setup"
+
+test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT
+
+stub_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
+calls="$test_tmp/calls.log"
+conf="$test_tmp/etc/modprobe.d/btusb-autosuspend.conf"
+mkdir -p "$stub_bin" "$test_tmp/dmi"
+
+cat >"$stub_bin/lspci" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+
+# Chatty like real lspci: keep writing well past the pipe buffer after the
+# match, so a grep -q consumer would kill this stub with SIGPIPE and pipefail
+# would read that as "no such hardware" (#6608).
+if (( ${T2_HARDWARE:-0} == 1 || ${BT_PCIE:-0} == 1 )); then
+  echo '04:00.0 Network controller [0280]: Broadcom Inc. Bluetooth [14e4:5fa0]'
+fi
+if (( ${T2_HARDWARE:-0} == 1 )); then
+  echo '01:00.0 Bridge [0680]: Apple Inc. T2 Security Chip [106b:1801]'
+fi
+if [[ -n ${WIFI_ID:-} ]]; then
+  echo "03:00.0 Network controller [0280]: Broadcom Inc. Wireless [14e4:$WIFI_ID]"
+fi
+for _ in {1..4096}; do
+  echo '02:00.0 Host bridge [0600]: Filler Device [ffff:0000]'
+done
+SH
+
+cat >"$stub_bin/sudo" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+
+printf 'sudo' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\t%s' "$@" >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\n' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+"$@"
+SH
+
+cat >"$stub_bin/omarchy-state" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+
+printf 'omarchy-state' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\t%s' "$@" >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\n' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+SH
+
+chmod +x "$stub_bin"/*
+
+run_leaf() {
+  local vendor="$1" wifi_id="${2:-}" t2="${3:-0}" bt_pcie="${4:-0}"
+  rm -rf "$test_tmp/etc"
+  mkdir -p "$test_tmp/etc"
+  printf '%s' "$vendor" >"$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor"
+
+  local script="$test_tmp/leaf.sh"
+  sed -e "s|/sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor|$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor|g" \
+      -e "s|/etc/modprobe.d|$test_tmp/etc/modprobe.d|g" \
+      "$leaf" >"$script"
+
+  WIFI_ID="$wifi_id" T2_HARDWARE="$t2" BT_PCIE="$bt_pcie" PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" \
+    bash -eE -o pipefail -c 'source "$1"' bash "$script" </dev/null
+}
+
+# T2 Bluetooth is PCIe (hci_bcm4377), not btusb -- this option has nothing to
+# act on there, and applying it would only cost battery on some other USB
+# device that happens to autosuspend.
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." 4488 1 >/dev/null
+[[ ! -f $conf ]] || fail "a T2 Mac is left alone; its Bluetooth isn't on btusb"
+pass "a T2 Mac is left alone; its Bluetooth isn't on btusb"
+
+# Apple Silicon Macs also run Bluetooth over PCIe (hci_bcm4377) with no T2
+# bridge chip at all -- the gate has to see that directly, not infer it from
+# T2's absence.
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." 4425 0 1 >/dev/null
+[[ ! -f $conf ]] || fail "an Apple Silicon Mac is left alone; its Bluetooth isn't on btusb either"
+pass "an Apple Silicon Mac is left alone; its Bluetooth isn't on btusb either"
+
+# A listed Wi-Fi ID with PCIe Bluetooth and no T2 bridge is the only shape where
+# the Bluetooth function's own ID and the old bridge proxy disagree.
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." 4464 0 1 >/dev/null
+[[ ! -f $conf ]] || fail "a Mac with a listed Wi-Fi part but PCIe Bluetooth is left alone"
+pass "a Mac with a listed Wi-Fi part but PCIe Bluetooth is left alone"
+
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." 4464 0 0 >/dev/null
+[[ -f $conf ]] || fail "the same Wi-Fi part with USB Bluetooth gets the quirk"
+pass "the same Wi-Fi part with USB Bluetooth gets the quirk"
+
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." 43ba 0 >/dev/null
+grep -qx 'options btusb enable_autosuspend=n' "$conf" 2>/dev/null ||
+  fail "a brcmfmac Mac without a T2 gets the quirk" "$(ls -R "$test_tmp/etc" 2>&1)"
+pass "a brcmfmac Mac without a T2 gets the quirk"
+
+# 2012-2015 Macs on the out-of-tree wl driver still have USB Bluetooth.
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." 43a0 0 >/dev/null
+[[ -f $conf ]] || fail "a BCM4360 Mac gets the quirk"
+pass "a BCM4360 Mac gets the quirk"
+
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." 4331 0 >/dev/null
+[[ -f $conf ]] || fail "a BCM4331 Mac gets the quirk"
+pass "a BCM4331 Mac gets the quirk"
+
+run_leaf "LENOVO" 43ba 0 >/dev/null
+[[ ! -f $conf ]] || fail "non-Apple hardware is left alone"
+pass "non-Apple hardware is left alone"
+
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." "" 0 >/dev/null
+[[ ! -f $conf ]] || fail "a Mac with no wireless device is left alone"
+pass "a Mac with no wireless device is left alone"
+
+run_migration() {
+  local vendor="$1" wifi_id="${2:-}" t2="${3:-0}" bt_pcie="${4:-0}"
+  printf '%s' "$vendor" >"$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor"
+  : >"$calls"
+
+  WIFI_ID="$wifi_id" T2_HARDWARE="$t2" BT_PCIE="$bt_pcie" PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" TEST_LOG="$calls" \
+    OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_DMI_VENDOR="$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor" \
+    OMARCHY_BTUSB_AUTOSUSPEND_CONF="$conf" \
+    bash -euo pipefail "$migration" >/dev/null
+}
+
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/etc"
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 43ba 0
+grep -qx 'options btusb enable_autosuspend=n' "$conf" 2>/dev/null ||
+  fail "the migration fixes an install that never got the quirk" "$(ls -R "$test_tmp/etc" 2>&1)"
+grep -Fq $'omarchy-state\tset\treboot-required' "$calls" ||
+  fail "the migration asks for the reboot that applies it" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration fixes an install that never got the quirk"
+
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 43ba 0
+(( $(grep -c 'enable_autosuspend=n' "$conf") == 1 )) ||
+  fail "the migration is idempotent" "$(cat "$conf")"
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] || fail "a repaired install is left untouched" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration is idempotent"
+
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/etc"
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 4488 1
+[[ ! -e $conf ]] || fail "the migration skips a T2 Mac" "$(cat "$conf")"
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] || fail "the migration escalates nothing on a T2 Mac" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration skips a T2 Mac; its Bluetooth isn't on btusb"
+
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/etc"
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 4425 0 1
+[[ ! -e $conf ]] || fail "the migration skips an Apple Silicon Mac" "$(cat "$conf")"
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] || fail "the migration escalates nothing on an Apple Silicon Mac" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration skips an Apple Silicon Mac; its Bluetooth isn't on btusb either"
+
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/etc"
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 4464 0 1
+[[ ! -e $conf ]] || fail "the migration skips a listed Wi-Fi part with PCIe Bluetooth" "$(cat "$conf")"
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] || fail "the migration escalates nothing there" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration skips a Mac with a listed Wi-Fi part but PCIe Bluetooth"
+
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/etc"
+run_migration "LENOVO" 43ba 0
+[[ ! -e $conf ]] || fail "the migration skips non-Apple hardware" "$(cat "$conf")"
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] || fail "the migration escalates nothing on unaffected hardware" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration skips hardware without USB-attached Broadcom Bluetooth"

comments.body:
Reviewed on a disposable VM. Both new suites pass — `test/shell.d/bluetooth-codec-test.sh` 8/8 and `test/shell.d/btusb-autosuspend-test.sh` 8/8, both exit 0 — and `./test/cli` is 116/116 with no failures. Bluetooth audio on Apple hardware cannot be exercised on a VM, so everything below about behaviour on real Macs is reasoned from the source, not observed. Nothing was pushed to your branch: the findings are design calls that are yours to make, not mine.

**The codec cap does not leak to non-Apple machines.** This was the thing most worth checking and it holds. I traced every consumer of `default/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/`: nothing copies `default/` wholesale into `~/.config`, nothing puts it on a WirePlumber or XDG search path, and the only two deployment paths for the fragment are the gated `cp` in `install/user/hardware/apple/fix-bluetooth-codec.sh` and the gated `cp` in `migrations/1787263050.sh`. Putting it under `default/` rather than `config/` is what makes that true — `config/` is the tree copied to every user, and `config/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/bluetooth-a2dp-autoconnect.conf` already lives there. A Framework or ThinkPad user with LDAC headphones is untouched.

**The gate keys on the Wi-Fi driver, but the fix targets the Bluetooth driver, and the two do not line up.** The predicate is copied verbatim from `install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh`, where it answers "does brcmfmac drive this machine's Wi-Fi". Here it is being asked "is this machine's Bluetooth on btusb", and it misses at both ends.

Too wide: on T2 Macs the internal Bluetooth is not on `btusb` at all. Omarchy itself loads the PCIe driver for it — `install/hardware/apple/fix-t2.sh:19` writes `hci_bcm4377` into `/etc/modules-load.d/t2.conf`, and `modinfo hci_bcm4377` on a current Arch kernel describes it as "Bluetooth support for Broadcom 4377/4378/4387/4388 devices". So for everything matched by the `106b:180[12]` arm, and for the `4464`/`4425`/`4433` IDs in the list, `options btusb enable_autosuspend=n` does nothing to the controller that is actually dropping audio. `migrations/1787262778.sh:22` still asks for a reboot to apply it, and `test/shell.d/btusb-autosuspend-test.sh:74` asserts "a T2 Mac gets the quirk" as though that were the intended outcome. Where the option is not inert on those machines it is acting on an external USB dongle instead, which is also where the battery cost lands.

Too narrow: the 2013–2015 Macs — BCM4360 and BCM4331, `14e4:43a0` and `14e4:4331`, handled separately in `install/hardware/fix-bcm43xx.sh` — are deliberately absent from the brcmfmac list because they run the out-of-tree `wl` driver. Their Bluetooth is still Broadcom over USB, which is exactly the population btusb autosuspend applies to, and they get neither fix.

Both halves ride one gate, but the btusb half and the codec half do not have the same target population. Splitting them, or gating the btusb half on the Bluetooth controller rather than the Wi-Fi one, looks like the shape of the answer — which machines each half is meant for is your call.

**The stated mechanism may not be what btusb does.** The comment at the top of `install/hardware/apple/fix-btusb-autosuspend.sh` says autosuspend "repeatedly powers the controller down and back up between transmissions". The knob itself checks out: `enable_autosuspend` is a real btusb bool parameter, `n` is a valid value, `CONFIG_BT_HCIBTUSB_AUTOSUSPEND=y` on Arch's kernel (verified on 7.1.8-arch1-3), and `btusb_open` releases its runtime-PM reference, so an open-but-idle controller can suspend. What I could not confirm is that this happens *during* an active A2DP stream rather than only across idle gaps. If you reproduced the dropouts and this option fixed them, please say so on the PR — that is worth more than either reading, and it would be good for the comment to match the mechanism.

**Six copies of one predicate.** `quattro` has two, the leaf and `migrations/1786391100.sh`; this PR takes it to six. #7577 is open right now to narrow that same nine-ID list, adding a `uname -m == x86_64` guard because `4425` and `4433` are Apple Silicon parts and Asahi reports `Apple Inc.` through DMI. If it lands, its guard reaches none of the four copies added here, and the codec cap would still truncate the codec list on an M-series Mac. An `omarchy-hw-*` helper would collapse all six, and the repo already has that convention.

**Smaller things, none blocking.** The file is named `bluez-prefer-sbc.conf` but its whole point is that AAC stays ahead of SBC; someone finding it later in `~/.config` will read the name and conclude the opposite. `bluez5.codecs` may need to be `override.bluez5.codecs` to replace rather than concatenate with another fragment's list — no effect on a stock Omarchy, where nothing else sets it. And the fragment goes to `~/.config` rather than `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}`, which matches `install/user/hardware/asus/fix-audio-mixer.sh` that this is modelled on, so that is a repo-wide inconsistency rather than something you introduced.

**What holds up.** The two migrations are correctly ordered and independent, both idempotent, both no-ops off Apple hardware, and both safe when `lspci` is missing. `[[ -f $conf ]] && exit 0` does not trip `errexit` under the runner's `bash -euo pipefail` — I checked that directly. Permissions are 0644 with no shebangs, `$OMARCHY_PATH` is exported into migrations by `omarchy-migrate`, `omarchy-state set reboot-required` matches the real interface, and `grep … >/dev/null` over `grep -q` is the right call under pipefail. Writing `/etc/modprobe.d` without sudo is correct, since `install/hardware/` runs as root. The env-var seams and the `sed` rewrite in the tests both follow `test/shell.d/brcmfmac-supplicant-test.sh`.

**Merge conflict.** #7671 adds a line at the same anchor in `install/hardware/all.sh`, immediately after `fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh`. A three-way merge of the two conflicts there. It is one line and resolves by keeping both, but whichever lands second has to do it.

A second reviewer (codex at xhigh) went over this independently; its independence is not currently guaranteed, so where we agreed I have said only that we agreed. It contributed two things I had not reasoned about and that I then verified myself: the T2/`hci_bcm4377` transport mismatch and the BCM4360 exclusion. It also read `grep -q '\baac\b'` in the codec test as vacuous; that one does not hold — grep is case-sensitive there and the only lowercase `aac` is on the codec line itself, so gutting the list to `[ sbc ]` does fail the assertion.

Waiting on you for how the two halves should be gated, and on the maintainer for whether dropping aptX and LDAC on every Mac is the trade to make — that part is a product decision rather than a bug.
@omarchybot run again, I made changes based on your comments.

Re-reviewed at a1c4e5b. On a disposable VM: `./test/cli` 116/116, `test/shell.d/bluetooth-codec-test.sh` 8/8, `test/shell.d/btusb-autosuspend-test.sh` 11/11, all exit 0. I also mutated the branch on that VM to check the new assertions have teeth — dropping `43a0|4331` from the inclusion list fails "a BCM4360 Mac gets the quirk", and deleting the T2 exclusion fails "a T2 Mac is left alone" — so the behaviour you added is genuinely covered. Nothing pushed to your branch: what is left is a design call, not a defect I should decide for you. Only what changed is below; the rest of the last review still stands as written.

**What the amendment fixed.** BCM4360 and BCM4331 (`14e4:43a0`, `14e4:4331`) now get the autosuspend quirk, which closes the "too narrow" half. The rename to `bluez-codec-cap.conf` fixes the name that said the opposite of what the file does. And the new `exit 0` guard is safe despite `AGENTS.md` warning that `install/` scripts may be sourced — `run_logged` runs each leaf as its own `bash -c 'source "$1"'` process at `install/helpers/logging.sh:54-64`, so it cannot cut the rest of hardware setup short. I checked that specifically because an early `exit` in a sourced leaf would have been much worse than the bug it was added for.

**The gate still decides a Bluetooth question from a Wi-Fi PCI ID, and that is the part that did not move.** Three facts from a current Arch kernel, 7.1.8-arch1-3, which I read off the running system rather than inferring:

- `hci_bcm4377` binds PCI `14e4:5fa0`, `5f69`, `5f71` and `5f72`. Those are Bluetooth-function IDs, and they are disjoint from every ID either gate matches. Its description is "Bluetooth support for Broadcom 4377/4378/4387/4388 devices".
- `hci_uart` carries 169 Broadcom ACPI IDs (`BCM2E00` upward). Broadcom Bluetooth over UART is a third transport, bound by neither `btusb` nor `hci_bcm4377`.
- `CONFIG_BT_HCIBTUSB_AUTOSUSPEND=y`, so on the machines that *are* on `btusb` the knob is real and does something.

So the transport is a property of the Bluetooth function, and neither the Wi-Fi PCI ID nor the T2 bridge ID `106b:180[12]` is that function. Swapping one proxy for another does not fix that. Concretely, where the btusb gate now lands:

- **Fires, and looks right:** `4331`, `43a0`, `43ba/43bb/43bc`, `43a3`, `43dc`. Whether each of those Macs really has USB Bluetooth is inference from the parts, not something I can observe on a VM.
- **Fires and should not:** Apple Silicon Macs. `14e4:4425` and `14e4:4433` are in the list, Asahi reports `Apple Inc.` through DMI and carries no T2 PCI ID (this is the whole subject of #7577), so the exclusion misses them and the gate opens. Their Bluetooth is `hci_bcm4377` on PCIe. Harmless for `btusb`, which is a module option with nothing to act on — but the codec cap has no architecture guard either, and there it strips aptX and LDAC from a machine whose Bluetooth controller is not the one this PR is about.
- **Never fires:** `14e4:4488`. `install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh:18` puts BCM4377 in "the T2 era on", so every machine carrying it also carries `106b:180[12]` and exits at line 13. Dead entry in the list.
- **Splits on the same chip:** `14e4:4464` is BCM4364. On a T2 machine the script exits at line 13; on the T2-less iMac19,1/19,2 it reaches line 22 and fires. Same Wi-Fi part, opposite answer, decided by a bridge chip that is not the Bluetooth controller. One of those two branches is wrong and the ID cannot tell you which.

If you want to keep this gated on hardware rather than on a model list, `lspci -nn | grep -E "14e4:(5fa0|5f69|5f71|5f72)"` asks the question directly: it is the PCIe Bluetooth function, so a match means the internal controller is not on `btusb`. That is a suggestion, not a request — which machines each half targets is still yours and the maintainer's call.

**The two halves now target different machines, and the files argue against the split.** `43a0` and `4331` get the autosuspend quirk but not the codec cap. `install/user/hardware/apple/fix-bluetooth-codec.sh:3-4` says the cap "covers Bluetooth over any transport ... since codec negotiation happens over the Bluetooth link itself", and `bluez-codec-cap.conf:2-5` blames Broadcom controllers under Wi-Fi/Bluetooth antenna contention generally. By both of those, a 2013-2015 BCM4360 MacBook is squarely in scope — and it is the machine with the single shared antenna your first description named. It now gets one half of the fix. That may be deliberate, but nothing in the branch says so.

**Still open from last time, unchanged:** the Apple Silicon codec truncation above; `bluez5.codecs` versus `override.bluez5.codecs`, which is inert on a stock Omarchy because nothing else sets the key (the only other shipped Bluetooth fragment, `config/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/bluetooth-a2dp-autoconnect.conf`, sets `monitor.bluez.rules`, a different key); the predicate now existing in six copies on this branch; and the question for the maintainer of whether dropping aptX and LDAC on every Mac is the right trade.

**Merge conflict, unchanged.** #7671 adds its line at the same anchor in `install/hardware/all.sh`, right after `fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh`. Whichever lands second resolves it by keeping both lines.

A second reviewer (codex at xhigh) went over the amended branch independently; its independence is not currently guaranteed, so where we agreed I say only that we agreed — that covers the Apple Silicon false positive and the `4464` split. It contributed three things I had not reasoned about. The UART transport, which I then verified above and which matters because it means a Wi-Fi ID cannot select for `btusb` even among non-T2 Intel Macs. That the non-T2 iMac19,1/19,2 may itself be on `hci_bcm4377`, which if true flips `4464` from a false negative on T2 machines to a false positive on the iMacs — I could not settle that either way, and it is a good reason not to settle it with this ID. And that `14e4:4434` (BCM4388) is in neither list. It also read the codec test's `bluez5.codecs`/`aac` assertions as vacuous; that does not hold, and I checked rather than argued — gutting the fragment to its comment block on the VM fails "the fragment keeps AAC so working devices like AirPods are not downgraded", because `grep -q '\baac\b'` is case-sensitive and the only lowercase `aac` is on the codec line. Its claim that `bluez5.codecs` is an enabled-set rather than an ordered preference, which would make the "AAC stays first" comment wrong, I could not verify: WirePlumber's bluez5 module is not installed on the test VM. Worth a look before that comment ships.

Waiting on you for how the two halves should be gated and whether the split between them is intended, and on the maintainer for the aptX/LDAC trade.

@omarchybot Thanks for the re-review — addressed the direct-detection suggestion:

  Gate now checks Bluetooth transport directly, not by proxy. Both the btusb autosuspend fix and its migration now match the Bluetooth function's own
  PCI ID (14e4:5fa0|5f69|5f71|5f72, hci_bcm4377) instead of inferring "not on btusb" from T2 bridge presence. This fixes the false negative on Apple
  Silicon Macs (which have PCIe Bluetooth with no T2 bridge at all) and resolves the BCM4364/4464 split on its own merits per machine instead of
  guessing from bridge presence.

  Dropped 14e4:4425/4433 (Apple Silicon Wi-Fi IDs) from both inclusion lists. They're a different Bluetooth chip generation than this fix is about;
  for the codec cap this was the actual bug, since that fix has no transport check to catch them incidentally.

  Added 14e4:43a0/4331 (2013–2015 BCM4360/4331 MacBooks — the antenna-shared machines from the original report) to the codec-cap list. They already
  got the btusb quirk but not the codec cap, with nothing in the branch explaining the split; there wasn't a reason for it, so both fixes now cover
  that hardware class.

  Left unchanged, as you flagged as discretionary:
  - Predicate still duplicated across six spots — no shared omarchy-hw-* helper added.
  - No UART (hci_uart) detection — no evidence any machine in either PCI ID list uses that transport.
  - bluez5.codecs vs override.bluez5.codecs — inert on stock Omarchy today (nothing else sets the key), left as-is.
  - install/hardware/all.sh insertion point still collides with #7671 at the same anchor — not resolved, whoever merges second picks up both lines
    fine.
  - aptX/LDAC dropped repo-wide on affected Macs — still a maintainer call, not changed.

  Tests updated: added an Apple Silicon exclusion case to both suites, BCM4360/4331 inclusion cases to the codec-cap suite.
  test/shell.d/btusb-autosuspend-test.sh 13/13, test/shell.d/bluetooth-codec-test.sh 11/11, bash -n clean on all six touched files. Amended into the
  original commit (7cc34682) rather than stacking a fixup, since this is all one coherent gate-correctness fix.

Re-reviewed the amendment at 7cc34682. The branch was force-pushed, so this covers everything new since a1c4e5b; the rest of the last review stands as written and only what changed is below. On a disposable VM at your head: `./test/cli` 116/116, `btusb-autosuspend-test.sh` 13/13, `bluetooth-codec-test.sh` 11/11, all exit 0.

**The gate change is right, and it fixes more than you claimed.** I ran both migrations on the VM against stubbed hardware, one machine shape at a time. The fragment now lands where it should: Apple Silicon no, T2 with PCIe Bluetooth no, non-Apple no, a listed Wi-Fi part with USB Bluetooth yes — and the case that mattered, `14e4:4464` with PCIe Bluetooth is skipped while the same Wi-Fi part with USB Bluetooth gets the quirk. That is the `4464` split closed on evidence instead of on a guess about which machine it is.

The part you did not claim: **T2 Macs are not all on `hci_bcm4377`.** On a current Arch kernel, 7.1.8-arch1-3, `btbcm` carries a DMI product table naming MacBookAir8,1 and 8,2, MacBookPro16,1, 16,2 and 16,4, and iMac20,1 and 20,2 — all T2 machines — and `btusb` depends on `btbcm` while `hci_bcm4377` depends only on `bluetooth`. Those T2 Macs have USB Bluetooth, and the old bridge-ID exclusion skipped every one of them. Your new gate gives them the fix, and it retires the "`14e4:4488` never fires" finding from last time: those are exactly the machines it fires on now. That is a population the previous review had wrong, and it is the strongest argument for the change you made.

**The codec cap's Apple Silicon truncation is fixed; the rationale that replaced it is not self-consistent.** Dropping `4425`/`4433` closes it — verified, the migration writes nothing on a stubbed Apple Silicon machine. But `install/user/hardware/apple/fix-bluetooth-codec.sh:7-9` excludes Apple Silicon because its Bluetooth is "a newer chip generation (4377/4378/4387/4388) this fix isn't about", while line 12 includes every T2 machine — and `install/hardware/apple/fix-t2.sh:19` together with your own new exclusion list puts T2 Bluetooth in that same generation when it is on PCIe, and on plain `btusb` otherwise. So the cap fires on a BCM4377 in a T2 Mac and not on a BCM4377 in an Apple Silicon Mac, for a reason that cannot tell the two apart. Line 5's "T2 Macs (PCIe hci_bcm4377)" is wrong for the machines above for the same reason. Whether the fix is to drop the T2 clause or to put Apple Silicon back is a hardware call I should not make for you — and `bluez-codec-cap.conf:2-3` still names "Apple Silicon-era MacBooks" as the affected population, so whichever way it goes, that line has to agree.

**Pushed one commit, e850c523.** Your two new Apple Silicon cases do not test the gate you changed. I reverted `fix-btusb-autosuspend.sh:17` and `migrations/1787262778.sh:9` to the old `106b:180[12]` proxy on the VM and the file still passed 13/13 — `4425` was dropped from the inclusion list in the same change, so that machine is skipped before it ever reaches the exclusion. `14e4:4464` is on the inclusion list and appears both with and without a bridge, so it is the one shape where the two gates disagree; with it, the same revert fails. Three assertions added in your file and style, 16/16 at the new head, `./test/cli` still 116/116 after.

Still open, and yours or the maintainer's to settle rather than defects I should push: the inclusion half is still a Wi-Fi ID list, so it can still miss a Mac with USB Bluetooth whose Wi-Fi part is not on it; the predicate is in six copies on the branch; `install/hardware/all.sh` still collides with #7671, which at its own head f81f4d52 adds its line at the same anchor, resolved by keeping both lines; and whether dropping aptX and LDAC on every affected Mac is the right trade is still a product decision.

Reviewed by Claude Opus 5, with codex at xhigh as an independent second opinion. Codex's independence is not currently guaranteed, so where we agreed I claim no more than agreement: it reached the vacuous-test finding on its own, which I had proved by mutation on the VM. It contributed the mixed T2 Bluetooth transport above, which I then verified against the kernel modules rather than taking on its word, and one thing neither of us could settle — that current Asahi U-Boot generates SMBIOS with a lowercase `apple` vendor, which would fail the case-sensitive `Apple*` test in every one of these scripts. That is inference from source, not an observation of a machine, and nothing here now depends on it. It found no high or medium functional defect. I rejected its suggestion to add cases for `4433` and the other three PCIe Bluetooth IDs as a nitpick.

## Pull request overview Adds Mac-specific mitigations for Bluetooth audio dropouts on Broadcom hardware. **Changes:** - Disables `btusb` autosuspend. - Restricts WirePlumber Bluetooth codecs to AAC and SBC variants. - Adds install hooks and migrations for new and existing systems. > [!TIP] > If you aren't ready for review, convert to a draft PR. > Click "Convert to draft" or run `gh pr ready --undo`. > Click "Ready for review" or run `gh pr ready` to reengage. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 7 out of 7 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `migrations/1787263050.sh` | Migrates the WirePlumber codec configuration. | | `migrations/1787262778.sh` | Migrates the `btusb` autosuspend setting. | | `install/user/hardware/apple/fix-bluetooth-codec.sh` | Installs the per-user codec fragment. | | `install/user/all.sh` | Runs the new user-level hardware fix. | | `install/hardware/apple/fix-btusb-autosuspend.sh` | Installs the kernel module option. | | `install/hardware/all.sh` | Runs the new system-level hardware fix. | | `default/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/bluez-prefer-sbc.conf` | Defines allowed Bluetooth codecs. |
Suppressed comments (1) **migrations/1787262778.sh:17** * Checking only for the file treats an empty, commented, or unrelated `btusb` configuration as if this quirk were active. Affected upgrades then skip both the option and the reboot request. Check for the active option and append it while preserving existing settings, as the analogous brcmfmac migration does. ``` [[ -f $conf ]] && exit 0 ```
--- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. Learn more in the docs.

## Pull request overview

Copilot reviewed 9 out of 9 changed files in this pull request and generated no new comments.




<details>
<summary>Suppressed comments (2)</summary>

**default/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/bluez-prefer-sbc.conf:10**
* `bluez5.codecs` only enables codecs; it does not preserve this array's order. PipeWire converts it to a lookup dictionary and applies its internal codec order, where SBC precedes SBC-XQ, so devices without AAC will not use the advertised AAC → SBC-XQ → SBC fallback. Add a WirePlumber profile-priority rule for the intended order while retaining this whitelist.
```
  bluez5.codecs = [ aac, sbc_xq, sbc ]
```
**migrations/1787262778.sh:20**
* Checking only for the file makes the migration skip the actual repair when this conventional config filename already exists—for example, with unrelated btusb options or `enable_autosuspend=y`. Detect the desired active option instead and append it when absent so existing settings are preserved and the migration reaches the required state.
```
[[ -f $conf ]] && exit 0

sudo mkdir -p "$(dirname "$conf")"
echo "options btusb enable_autosuspend=n" | sudo tee "$conf" >/dev/null
```
</details>

In particular, if the autosuspend config already exists, the preceding migration exits without requesting a reboot, leaving this change inactive until a later login. Restart the user audio service after the copy or explicitly request a reboot.
